featured_charts.title: World of Debt
featured_charts.description: Developing countries’ public debt continues to grow. The main problem is how much it costs them. They pay far higher interest rates than developed ones. In many, interest bills now exceed spending on health or education.

solutions.title: UNCTAD's work on debt
solutions.description: Borrowing lets governments invest in roads, schools and hospitals. But when interest costs rise faster than revenue, there’s less money to invest in people and their future. That’s now the case for a growing number of developing countries.

borrowers_platform.title: No country can solve the debt crisis alone
borrowers_platform.description: Lenders have long coordinated among themselves. Borrowing countries now have a platform to share experience, learn from each other and strengthen their voice in global debt discussions.

dmfas_highlight.title: Countries can’t manage debt they can’t measure
dmfas_highlight.description: Until recently, South Sudan tracked its loans in spreadsheets. In 2025, it became the second country to install the latest version of UNCTAD’s debt-management software. The DMFAS programme also trains debt officers and advises governments, so borrowing decisions rest on reliable data.
